newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus president sacks close aide.
newsitem.headline: Belarus president sacks close aide.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko, continuing a political shake-up in Belarus, on Thursday sacked a close aide and supporter of his policy of integrating with Russia, a presidential administration source said.
Vladimir Zametalin was dismissed as deputy head of Lukashenko's administration following a presidential decree and put in charge of the state press committee, the source said.

Zametalin pushed pan-Slavist ideals and a pro-Russian stance which helped win Lukashenko victories in a presidential election in 1994 and referendums which have given him sweeping powers and have drawn sharp criticism from the West.
Lukashenko has complained of slow progress in moving closer to Russia since he and President Boris Yeltsin signed a deal last April on integration between the neighbouring Slav states.

Lukashenko has drawn widespread criticism for his hardline policies which have muzzled the press, clamped down on independent trade unions and slowed reforms in the former Soviet republic of 10 million on Russia's western flank.
Since he won wide powers in a November 24 referendum which critics said was fraudulent, several ministers have been replaced and other officials sacked.
